Ticket Management: Creating a ticket with every field omitted still succeeds, applying sensible defaults for category, priority, title, and description; only a TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR caller can reach this endpoint at all.
column3:
1. Log in as a TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR — TicketController carries a class-level @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('TRAINER','ADMINISTRATOR')"), so every other role (including LEARNER and COURSE_MANAGER) is rejected before reaching any handler (see TICKET_FT18).
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets body {} (no category/priority/title/description).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned TicketResponseDTO's default field values.
column4: 1. 200 OK; TicketResponseDTO with priority="MEDIUM", category="GENERAL_ENQUIRY", title="Support Request", description="No details provided.", status="PENDING", a generated ticketCode ("#<hex timestamp>"). No first TicketMessage row is auto-created for the thread (createTicket no longer does this).
column5: - Logged in as TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR (the only two roles this controller accepts).

Ticket Management: Ticket category has no create-time whitelist — any string is accepted and persisted verbatim, even values normally reserved for staff-only routing.
column3:
1. Log in as a TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets body {"category":"not_a_real_category"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned category field.
column4: 1. 200 OK; the ticket is created with category="not_a_real_category" as literally supplied — no validation error.
column5: - Logged in as TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR.

Ticket Management: A user can edit their own ticket's title/description, while a different Trainer editing another user's ticket is masked to a generic 500 instead of a clean 403.
column3:
1. Log in as the TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR owner of an existing ticket and prepare PUT /api/v1/tickets/{ownTicketId} body {"title":"Updated title"}; send it and confirm the title changed.
2. Log out and log in as a different TRAINER account that does not own the ticket (a LEARNER/COURSE_MANAGER would be rejected earlier by the controller's own TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR-only gate and never reach this check — see TICKET_FT18).
3. Prepare and send PUT /api/v1/tickets/{theOtherUsersTicketId} body {"title":"hacked"}.
4. Inspect the second response's status.
column4:
1. Step 1: 200 OK, title updated.
2. Steps 2-4: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real "Unauthorized to update this ticket" RuntimeException never reaches the client as a clean 403.
column5: - A ticket owned by a different TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR user exists for step 2.

Ticket Management: Viewing a ticket's full detail is allowed for its owner or an Administrator; every other caller is denied, but with two different shapes of denial depending on how far they get.
column3:
1. Log in as the ticket's TRAINER owner and prepare/send GET /api/v1/tickets/{id}; confirm it returns full detail with messages[].
2. Log in as an ADMINISTRATOR (not the owner) and repeat the same GET.
3. Log in as a different TRAINER (not the owner, not ADMINISTRATOR) and repeat the same GET.
4. Log in as a LEARNER and repeat the same GET.
5. Compare all four response statuses.
column4:
1. Steps 1-2: 200 OK, full detail with messages[].
2. Step 3: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — TicketServiceImpl.getTicketDetail's isStaff check only treats a role literally "ADMINISTRATOR" (case-insensitive) or containing "ADMIN" as staff, so a plain TRAINER is neither the owner nor staff and hits the unmasked "Access denied" RuntimeException. COURSE_MANAGER/TRAINER_LEAD would fail the same way if they could reach this endpoint at all — they can't (see step 4).
3. Step 4: 403 Forbidden, clean — rejected before reaching the service by TicketController's class-level @PreAuthorize("hasAnyRole('TRAINER','ADMINISTRATOR')"), which blocks LEARNER outright (and would equally block COURSE_MANAGER).
column5: - A ticket exists, owned by a TRAINER; a second, unrelated TRAINER account, an ADMINISTRATOR account, and a LEARNER account are all available for steps 2-4.

Ticket Management: A Trainer can list their own tickets, filterable by status including the special "PROCESSED" alias that maps to both terminal states.
column3:
1. Log in as a TRAINER with tickets in multiple statuses (some APPROVED, some REJECTED, some still PENDING/PROCESSING) — a plain LEARNER cannot reach this endpoint at all, since TicketController is TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR-only (see TICKET_FT18).
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/tickets/my-tickets?status=PROCESSED.
3. Inspect the returned list.
4. Confirm every returned ticket's status is either APPROVED or REJECTED, and none are PENDING/PROCESSING.
column4: 1. 200 OK; only tickets whose status is APPROVED or REJECTED are returned (PROCESSED is a virtual filter mapping to both terminal states).
column5: - Logged in as TRAINER or ADMINISTRATOR; tickets in multiple statuses exist for the caller.

Ticket Management: The ticket owner can add a follow-up message to their own ticket's thread.
column3:
1. Log in as the TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR owner of an existing ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/tickets/{ownTicketId}/messages body {"message":"Any update on this?"}.
3. Send the request.
4. GET the ticket's detail to confirm the message now appears in the thread.
column4: 1. 200 OK; TicketMessageDTO returned, appended to the thread. Because the sender isn't recognized as staff, an "ADMINISTRATOR"-role broadcast notification (TicketResponse) also fires even though this was the owner's own message, not a staff reply.
column5: - Logged in as the TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR owner of an existing ticket.

Ticket Management: Fixed IDOR: an unrelated Trainer can no longer post into another user's ticket thread — addMessage now enforces a real ownership-or-staff check that did NOT exist before, throwing an "Access denied" error (masked to a generic 500) instead of silently succeeding.
column3:
1. Log in as Trainer X and create a ticket (Ticket A); note its id.
2. Log out and log in as unrelated Trainer Y — not staff (not ADMINISTRATOR/ADMIN-named), not the owner of Ticket A. (A LEARNER couldn't even reach this endpoint, since TicketController itself is TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR-only — see TICKET_FT18 — so Y must be a TRAINER to actually exercise this check.)
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/tickets/{A's id}/messages body {"message":"I can see this thread"} as Trainer Y.
4. Inspect the response status/body.
5. Log back in as Trainer X and GET /api/v1/tickets/{A's id} to confirm Y's message was NOT added.
column4:
1. Step 3: 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — the real "Access denied: You do not have permission to reply to this ticket" RuntimeException is thrown and never surfaced as a clean 403.
2. Step 5: Y's message is ABSENT from X's ticket thread — confirming the write was rejected, not just the error message being wrong. This reverses the previously-confirmed IDOR in this same test case: the cross-account write path is now blocked, not just poorly reported.
column5: - Two unrelated TRAINER accounts, X (ticket owner) and Y (unrelated, non-ADMINISTRATOR).

Ticket Management: An Administrator's reply auto-transitions a PENDING ticket to PROCESSING, while the ticket owner's own follow-up messages never trigger this transition.
column3:
1. Log in as the TRAINER owner of a fresh PENDING ticket and add a message to it; confirm the status stays PENDING.
2. Log in as an ADMINISTRATOR — the only role both TicketController's class-level gate and TicketServiceImpl.addMessage's isStaff check recognize for replying to someone else's ticket; a COURSE_MANAGER/TRAINER_LEAD account cannot reach TicketController at all (see TICKET_FT18) — and add a reply to the same ticket.
3. Inspect the ticket's status after the ADMINISTRATOR's reply.
column4:
1. Step 1: status remains PENDING after the owner's own message.
2. Steps 2-3: status flips to PROCESSING after the ADMINISTRATOR's reply.
column5: - A fresh PENDING ticket exists, owned by a TRAINER; an ADMINISTRATOR account is available.

Ticket Management: Staff can list and filter the management queue by status, category, and keyword together, and the results narrow correctly.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR (the only role granted the MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES authority by default; a COURSE_MANAGER/TRAINER_LEAD account must be explicitly granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES via Roles & Permissions first, or it gets 403 — see TICKET_FT18) in an environment with multiple, distinguishable tickets.
2. Prepare GET /api/v1/management/tickets?status=PENDING&category=GENERAL_ENQUIRY&keyword=<part of a known ticket's title or requester's name>.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the returned list and confirm every entry matches all three filters.
column4: 1. 200 OK; results correctly narrowed by all three filters combined.
column5: - ADMINISTRATOR logged in (or a role explicitly granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES); multiple tickets exist with distinguishable titles/requesters.

Ticket Management: Staff approves a ticket without supplying a custom response, and a sensible default response is applied automatically.
column3:
1. Log in as ADMINISTRATOR (or a role granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES) and identify a processable ticket (not PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST — see TICKET_FT12 for the current, unrestricted state of that rule).
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"APPROVE"} (no adminResponse).
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's resulting status/adminResponse and confirm the owner was notified.
column4: 1. 200 OK; status=APPROVED, adminResponse="Ticket approved by administrator." (wording changed from the previously-documented "by manager."); processedBy/processedAt set; the ticket owner is notified (TicketReviewed).
column5: - Staff logged in; a PENDING/PROCESSING ticket exists.

Ticket Management: Staff rejects a ticket while supplying a custom rejection reason, and that reason is persisted on the ticket.
column3:
1. Log in as staff and identify a processable ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"REJECT","rejectionReason":"Not a valid request"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's resulting status/rejectionReason.
column4: 1. 200 OK; status=REJECTED, rejectionReason="Not a valid request"; owner notified. Note: adminResponse is always returned as null for a REJECTED ticket regardless of what was supplied — mapToDTO unconditionally scrubs it whenever status=REJECTED.
column5: - Staff logged in; a processable ticket exists.

Ticket Management: Confirmed, still-open gap (do not fix in code — flag only): the PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST authorization rule has been REMOVED from processTicket, not merely masked — any caller who passes ManagementTicketController's own @PreAuthorize (by default only ADMINISTRATOR, or any role explicitly granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES) can now approve/reject these tickets, including a Course Manager.
column3:
1. Via a direct HTTP call (bypassing the UI, which never lets a user pick this category), create a ticket with category="REFUND_REQUEST".
2. Log in as a COURSE_MANAGER that has been granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES (not otherwise an ADMINISTRATOR).
3. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"APPROVE"}.
4. Inspect the response status/body, then GET the ticket again.
column4:
1. Step 3: 200 OK — the request SUCCEEDS. TicketServiceImpl.processTicket no longer contains any category/role check for PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE/REFUND_REQUEST (the code has a conspicuous blank gap where such a check used to sit).
2. Step 4: the ticket's status IS now APPROVED — a non-Administrator manager was able to approve a Bank/Tax-Info or Refund ticket that the business rule previously reserved for System Admin. This is a real, currently-live authorization gap; it is flagged here for follow-up, not fixed as part of this documentation pass.
column5: - A REFUND_REQUEST or PAYOUT_INFO_UPDATE category ticket exists (create via direct HTTP call, bypassing the UI); caller is a COURSE_MANAGER granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES but not ADMINISTRATOR.

Ticket Management: Submitting an unrecognized process action value leaves the ticket's actual status/response fields unchanged, yet still sends the owner a misleading "Support Ticket Rejected" notification with "Reason: N/A".
column3:
1. Log in as staff and identify a processable ticket.
2. Prepare POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process body {"action":"MAYBE"}.
3. Send the request.
4. Inspect the ticket's status/adminResponse/rejectionReason (should be unchanged) and the owner's notification inbox.
column4: 1. 200 OK — the ticket's status/adminResponse/rejectionReason are all UNCHANGED from before the call (neither the APPROVE nor REJECT branch matches an unrecognized action), though processedBy/processedAt ARE still overwritten. No message is appended to the ticket's thread (processTicket never writes a TicketMessage in the current code). The owner nonetheless receives a "Support Ticket Rejected" notification with body "Ticket rejected. Reason: N/A" — misleading, since the ticket was never actually rejected.
column5: - Staff logged in; a processable ticket exists.

Ticket Management: Ticket creation only notifies the ADMINISTRATOR role — neither a Course-Manager/"Trainer Lead"-only account nor any other non-Administrator staff account is notified, even one explicitly granted permission to process tickets.
column3:
1. Prepare two staff test accounts: one holding only ADMINISTRATOR, one holding only COURSE_MANAGER (granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES so it CAN process tickets via TICKET_FT09-12, but holds no ADMINISTRATOR-named role).
2. As a TRAINER, create a new ticket.
3. Log in as the ADMINISTRATOR account and check its notification inbox.
4. Log in as the COURSE_MANAGER account and check its notification inbox.
column4:
1. Step 3: the ADMINISTRATOR account receives a "TicketCreated" notification — TicketServiceImpl.createTicket calls notifyRole("ADMINISTRATOR", "TicketCreated", ...) directly.
2. Step 4: the COURSE_MANAGER account receives NONE for this event, despite being fully able to open and process the same ticket from the management queue once granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES — a real coverage gap between who gets notified and who can act.
column5: - An ADMINISTRATOR account and a COURSE_MANAGER account (granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES, no ADMINISTRATOR-named role) both exist.

Ticket Management: A closed ticket (APPROVED/REJECTED) rejects further replies from anyone, including its own owner — enforced server-side, not just hidden behind the UI's "This ticket is closed" banner.
column3:
1. Log in as staff and approve or reject a PENDING ticket (per TICKET_FT10/FT11) so its status becomes APPROVED or REJECTED.
2. Log in as the ticket's TRAINER owner and prepare/send POST /api/v1/tickets/{id}/messages body {"message":"One more thing"}.
3. Inspect the response.
column4: 1. 500 Internal Server Error, generic masked body — TicketServiceImpl.addMessage throws "Cannot reply to a closed ticket" (a plain RuntimeException, never surfaced as a clean 4xx) whenever the ticket's status is APPROVED or REJECTED, even for the ticket's own owner.
column5: - A ticket has just been approved or rejected (status=APPROVED or REJECTED); logged in as its TRAINER owner.

Ticket Management: By default, a Course Manager account cannot reach either TicketController or the staff management queue — the MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES authority required by ManagementTicketController is seeded only to ADMINISTRATOR (RolePermissionDataInitializer gives COURSE_MANAGER only VIEW_PLATFORM_DASHBOARD and CREATE_AND_MANAGE_EXAMS_CM), and TicketController itself only ever accepts TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR.
column3:
1. Log in as a COURSE_MANAGER account that has NOT been separately granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES via Roles & Permissions (the default seeded state).
2. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/tickets/my-tickets (TicketController) with that account's Authorization header.
3. Prepare and send GET /api/v1/management/tickets (ManagementTicketController) with the same account.
4. Prepare and send POST /api/v1/management/tickets/{id}/process with the same account.
5. Inspect all response statuses.
column4:
1. Step 2: 403 Forbidden — TicketController's class-level @PreAuthorize only allows TRAINER/ADMINISTRATOR.
2. Steps 3-4: 403 Forbidden — ManagementTicketController requires MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES or ADMINISTRATOR, neither of which a default COURSE_MANAGER has. A COURSE_MANAGER must be explicitly granted MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES via Roles & Permissions before the staff ticket queue tests (TICKET_FT09-FT15) apply to it.
column5: - A COURSE_MANAGER account exists with only its default seeded permissions (no MANAGE_ACCOUNTS_ROLES grant).
